To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrical conductivity and soft thermal photon emissivity of QCD plasma are of order 1 / T, in agreement with expectations based on perturbation theory.
the electrical conductivity of the QCD phase transition at zero baryon chemical potential, as a function of temperature, is 0.1 at 1.5 T c, 0.5 at 2 T c, 1.0 at 2.5 T c and 3 at 3 T c.
the soft photon emissivity in the QCD plasma has a peak in the vicinity of T / T c = 1.5 and that the peak height is about 0.5 GeV 4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical conductivity in the QCD plasma at temperatures above the critical temperature.
the electrical conductivity and soft-photon emissivity of the quark-gluon plasma.
the electrical conductivity of a hot quark-gluon plasma, and the closely associated problem of the soft photon emissivity in the same medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conductivity and the emissivity of the plasma are finite at the phase transition, and are of order 1 / ( π T ) at T = 2 T c.
the soft photon emissivity in the hot phase is not zero, and the conductivity is finite, and is of order 1.5 × 10 − 3 for T = T c, and is of order unity at T ≫ T c.
the soft photon emissivity is consistent with the perturbative result at T / T c = 3, but is significantly larger at lower temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conductivity is found to be of order 0.5 at T / T c ≈ 1.5, and then rises steadily to 1 at T / T C ≈ 2.5.
the soft photon emissivity in the QCD plasma increases with the temperature, but that the rate of increase is not large.
the electrical conductivity of the QCD is of the order of 1 / 4 π T.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soft photon emissivity is not suppressed at temperatures T ⪆ T c, as is the case in the high temperature limit.
the electrical conductivity and soft-photon emissivity in the QCD plasma are significantly smaller than the values obtained in a free gas model.
, in the vicinity of T c, the electrical conductivity of QCD is of the same order of magnitude as in the weakly interacting theory, QED.
